Class IuJsonb

java.lang.Object
iu.client.jsonb.IuJsonb
All Implemented Interfaces:
jakarta.json.bind.Jsonb, AutoCloseable
public class IuJsonb extends Object implements jakarta.json.bind.Jsonb
Implements Jsonb over the IuJsonAdapter conversions, streaming through IuJsonAdapter.read(JsonParser) and IuJsonAdapter.write(Object, JsonGenerator).

Supports JsonbConfig.FORMATTING, JsonbConfig.NULL_VALUES, JsonbConfig.ENCODING, JsonbConfig.BINARY_DATA_STRATEGY (BinaryDataStrategy.BYTE by default), JsonbConfig.PROPERTY_NAMING_STRATEGY (every standard strategy, and PropertyNamingStrategy instances), JsonbConfig.PROPERTY_ORDER_STRATEGY, JsonbConfig.PROPERTY_VISIBILITY_STRATEGY, JsonbConfig.SERIALIZERS, JsonbConfig.DESERIALIZERS, and JsonbConfig.ADAPTERS, JsonbConfig.DATE_FORMAT and JsonbConfig.LOCALE, JsonbConfig.STRICT_IJSON, and JsonbConfig.CREATOR_PARAMETERS_REQUIRED, as well as IuJsonAdapter.SERIALIZATION_OPTIONS and IuJsonAdapter.BASE64_URL_UNPADDED. An enum converts as text by Enum.name().

A date format, from JsonbConfig.DATE_FORMAT or declared by @JsonbDateFormat, is a DateTimeFormatter pattern, or TIME_IN_MILLIS; see FormatAdapters. A declared format, on a property's accessor or field, then the class declaring it, then its package, wins over the configured one, even when it declares the default format. @JsonbNumberFormat writes a number as text in its DecimalFormat pattern, and reads that text or a number. A format replaces the built-in conversion, so configured components still run first.

A business object is created by the one constructor or static factory method declared @JsonbCreator, or a record by its canonical constructor, and otherwise by its no-arg constructor. A creator parameter reads the JSON name @JsonbProperty declares, or its Java name, compiled with -parameters, named as properties are; its annotations declare formats and components as a property's do. Reading holds the values until the object is read through, then creates the instance and sets the other properties. A parameter not read is null, a primitive's default, or an empty optional, unless JsonbConfig.CREATOR_PARAMETERS_REQUIRED. A record's components write by their accessors.

@JsonbTypeInfo and @JsonbSubtype convert polymorphic types. An instance writes, before its properties, a key and alias for each type in its type information chain, outermost first, and a value declared as a type with type information writes its runtime type's properties. Reading picks the subtype by the key of the type's own type information, else its nearest supertype's: directly from the parser when the key comes first, as written, else from the object read through. An object without the key reads as the declared type. Type information from unrelated types can't be merged, a key may appear only once in a chain, and no property may share its name.

JsonbConfig.STRICT_IJSON writes only an object or array at the top level, byte[] as base64url whatever else is configured, and dates without a format of their own as I-JSON requires: Date, Calendar, Instant, LocalDate, and LocalDateTime as an ISO date and time with an offset and seconds. Numbers are not restricted; the JSON-B specification leaves them out of strict I-JSON.

Serializers, deserializers, and adapters form chains: any number may be configured for a type, each applies to its type and every subtype, and they run from the most specific to the least, then in configured order. See IuJsonbValueAdapter for how control passes along a chain.

A component a type declares by @JsonbTypeAdapter, @JsonbTypeSerializer, or @JsonbTypeDeserializer joins the chains as if registered for the declaring type, so also applies to its subtypes, ahead of configured components that are no more specific. One a property declares, on its accessor or field, heads that property's chain; passed a value back, the context continues with the type's chain. Each declared component class is instantiated once per provider by its no-arg constructor.

A component registered for a broad type, such as Object, Comparable, or Serializable, doesn't apply to a scalar type: text, a number, or a boolean. It doesn't see a null declared as one of those types, nor a value written whose runtime type is one, nor a JSON string, number, or boolean read as any type. It does see a null of a type that isn't scalar, or that isn't known, as when a null is written without a type or passed to a context by a serializer that isn't already converting it. Other values written as text, such as dates, still reach broad components. Components registered for a scalar type, such as CharSequence, Number, or Boolean, apply to scalars as usual.

Thread-safe: every conversion runs as a call with its own IuSerializationContext or IuDeserializationContext, held per thread while it runs.

    • itemScope

      final ItemScope itemScope
      Names each array, collection, and map item in the path of the call in progress, so a failure reads as Root.items[2].name or Root.byName["k"].

      An item converted with no call in progress, as a lazy Iterable converts its items when iterated, tracks nothing; its own conversion starts a call of its own.

    • conversionType

      Type conversionType(Class<?> type)
      Gets the type a platform class converts as, for a class with no built-in conversion of its own, such as a JDK-internal collection or a subclass of a supported type.

      The nearest superclass with a built-in conversion is used, short of Object; failing that, the first of CharSequence, Map, List, Set, Collection, Iterable, Iterator, Enumeration, and Stream the class implements.

      Parameters:
      type - platform class
      Returns:
      type itself if it has a conversion of its own; the type it converts as; Object if none applies
